title: APA § 553: notice, participation, reasons, and publication
shortTitle: APA § 553: notice, participation, reasons, and publication
summary: Ordinary notice-and-comment rulemaking provides notice of a proposal, an opportunity for written participation, a statement of basis and purpose, and publication of the final rule.
notes:
Section 553 supplies the central procedural framework for informal rulemaking. The assigned introduction identifies general notice of the proposed action, an opportunity to submit data, views, or arguments, a concise general statement of basis and purpose, and publication of the resulting rule. Oral hearings and cross-examination are not universal requirements of this model. Exceptions and special organic-statute procedures require separate analysis.

Formal rulemaking, when triggered, uses §§ 556 and 557 or analogous statutory requirements and demands a trial-type evidentiary process. The reading describes the historical retreat from that model, including the costs and delays of food standards and wage-setting proceedings. But it preserves disagreement: defenders argue that testing expert assumptions and exposing the basis of predictions can improve policy; critics emphasize program abandonment, delay, and the displacement of agency initiative toward less constrained methods.

Later cases interpret meaningful participation and reasoned decision-making to require disclosure of important supporting studies, responses to significant comments, and a final rule within the logical range of the notice. Vermont Yankee limits judicial imposition of additional procedures beyond statutory and constitutional requirements. The tension is about the boundary of statutory interpretation, not a simple choice between unlimited judicial procedure and an agency free to ignore § 553.
